name: Iran nuclear programme
value: IAEA 13 Nov: no access, HEU unverified
summary: IAEA report on 13 Nov calls Iran's lack of access a proliferation concern; enriched uranium stock still unverified
state: An IAEA report circulated on 13 Nov says the lack of information on Iran's nuclear sites and material is a proliferation concern needing urgent action, and that inspectors still have no access to the Isfahan underground enrichment plant (Al Jazeera). The agency says it lost continuity of knowledge over Iran's highly enriched uranium, estimated at over 400 kg, more than a year ago (The National, 13 Nov). Iran says it stays in the NPT; no strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: The main exposure is through the wider Gulf conflict: energy prices, shipping and travel in the region. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice for Iran and neighbouring states.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed; ~400+ kg enriched uranium unverified (Watch); no strike, NPT exit or weaponisation (Alert not met)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — UN watchdog calls on Iran to reopen nuclear facilities to inspection
The National — IAEA expresses concern over Iranian underground uranium-enrichment plant

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
